references.text: Matthew's parallel to the parable of the sower: When anyone hears the word about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in their heart. This is the direct parallel to Luke's description of the seed by the path.
Mark's parallel: Those by the path are those who hear the word, but immediately Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them. Mark uses 'Satan' where Luke uses 'the devil'.

Paul writes that the gospel is hidden for those who are perishing, because the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel. This illuminates how the devil prevents people from believing and being saved.

The Lord opened Lydia's heart so she paid attention to what Paul said. This shows the contrast: God opens the heart to receive the word, while in Luke 8:12 the devil takes the word away from the heart.

Peter exhorts: Be sober-minded and alert! Your adversary, the devil, prowls around like a roaring lion seeking someone to devour. This confirms the devil's active role in opposing believers, just as he takes the word from the heart.
Paul says that Satan hindered him from coming to the Thessalonians. This shows Satan's active role in hindering God's word and God's work, consistent with Luke 8:12.

Jesus sends Paul to open people's eyes, turn them from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance by faith. Satan's power keeps people away from faith and salvation, as in Luke 8:12.

John quotes Isaiah saying that God has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so they cannot see or understand and turn back. This illuminates the theme that the heart is prevented from receiving God's word and believing.

The great dragon, the ancient serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world – this identifies the devil as one who actively opposes God's people and deceives humanity, in agreement with Luke 8:12.
The parable itself of the seed that fell by the path and was eaten by birds, which Jesus then explains in verse 19 as the devil snatching away the word. Parallel to Luke 8:5 and 8:12.
